assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about making all students do community service. I don't think it should be required, but I think the school should make it easier for kids to volunteer if they want to.

I understand why people like the idea. Some of my friends tutor little kids at the elementary school and they always come back happy. Some other kids pick up trash at the park on Saturdays and the park looks a lot better after. Those kids really care about our town.

But when you force people to do it, its different. Lots of kids in my grade already have homework, sports, jobs, and little brothers and sisters to watch. My friend works at night at a grocery store so her family can pay the rent. If she had to do service hours too, it would just be one more thing and she would probably be mad about it. Also, kids who only volunteer to get the hours done usually just do the bare minimum and don't really try.

There is another problem which is how it would work. Tutoring and cleanups need adults to plan them and watch everybody. If hundreds of students all need a spot at the same time, the school and the groups in town could get overwhelmed. Some kids would end up with jobs that are pointless and don't help anyone.

I think a better idea is to encourage service instead of forcing it. The school could have a volunteer fair where local groups come and students can sign up. You could also give awards at assemblies to students who do service, and let kids count the service they do at school events. If students find something they like doing, they will keep doing it even after they graduate.

Thank you for reading my letter. I hope our school can get students excited to help the community instead of just making them do it.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the idea that every student must do community service. I do not agree with making it a rule. I think the school should set up ways for students to volunteer if they choose to.

Some of my friends tutor kids at the elementary school on Tuesdays. Other students spend a Saturday picking up trash at the park. I see them at school on Monday and they talk about what they did that weekend. Those students do something for the town, and people notice it.

A requirement changes things. Many of my classmates already have homework, sports, jobs, and younger brothers or sisters to watch after school. One girl I know works nights at a grocery store so her family can pay rent. If the school gives her a number of hours to finish, that is one more item on her list. When a student volunteers just to check a box, they usually do the minimum. The people at the site can tell when a student is there only for the hours.

There is also the planning. Tutoring and park cleanups need adults to organize them. The adults who run these groups already have a lot to manage. If hundreds of students need a place to volunteer at the same time, the school and the local groups might run out of spots. Some students would end up doing busywork that serves no purpose.

My plan is to encourage service instead of ordering it. The school could hold a volunteer fair where local groups set up tables and students sign up. Teachers could announce the names of volunteers at assemblies. Service done at school events could count too, so students do not need to find extra time. A student who picks an activity on their own will probably keep doing it after graduation.

I am asking the school to consider this plan. It would give students a choice and still send more of them to volunteer sites.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
